title: The lion and the mouse.
lines: In a hot country, on the wide savannah, a lion lay sleeping under a tree.
He was the king of all the animals.
He had a big golden mane around his head, and sharp teeth, and when he roared, the ground shook.
A little grey mouse came by.
She wasn't paying attention, and oops, she ran right over the lion's nose.
With one paw he caught the mouse.
Who dares to wake me up?
Oh, please, great king, let me go!
I'm not even a mouthful for you.
And if you let me go, one day I'll help you too.
The lion began to laugh loudly.
A tiny little mouse can't help a big lion!
But he laughed so hard that he lifted his paw.
A few days later the lion went hunting in the forest.
But hunters had put up a big net between the trees.
He pulled, he bit, he rolled.
But the more he moved, the more tangled he got.
Then the lion roared as loudly as he could.
But the little mouse heard it too.
And she ran as fast as she could to the lion.
Don't be afraid, said the mouse.
And the mouse began to nibble the ropes of the net.
With her small sharp teeth she bit through rope after rope.
It took a long time, but she didn't give up.
The lion looked at the little mouse.
I laughed at you, he said, because you were so small.
And from that day on the lion and the mouse were the very best of friends.
Because even the smallest can be great.
